items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: I made an effort to distance myself from that influence, from Scott’s influence.

ctx.x: You grew up in a time where you could have, in your early years as a saxophonist, you could have been listening to Grover Washington and that kind of saxophone, but that didn’t get you, huh?

No it didn’t. Actually when I was first starting to play saxophone, a friend, a saxophone player from Rhode Island where I’m from, suggested I pick up a Scott Hamilton record. So I bought a Scott Hamilton record and I heard the great big sound he had, and I said well that’s what I want to sound like.
That was really it then, huh?
